text: Different business units often need different versions of the same kind of policy — one country's payment terms aren't another's. Oracle Fusion solves this with reference data sets.

Oracle Fusion is one piece of software shared by every business unit, but they frequently need different values for the same kind of setup data. Without separation, every unit would be forced onto identical policies.

A reference data set is a named grouping of reference data values. Payment terms can be partitioned by set — a US Policies set and an EU Policies set, each with its own list. A business unit is assigned to a specific set for each type it uses.

Not every piece of data needs a business-unit-specific version. The Common Set, sometimes called the Enterprise Set, holds data every business unit should see the same way. Over-segmenting adds unnecessary maintenance.

The system identifies which set applies using a determinant, usually the business unit. A reference data set is a named grouping a business unit is assigned to. Next up, lesson thirteen: shared and non-shared reference data.
